answer: In a marketplace where agents sell mesa maps, shale surveys, and ember alerts, voting power over shared funds is proportional to tokens locked for 30 days, rather than the number of accounts. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand fake agents gives the attacker exactly the same voting power as locking them in one account. To gain more influence, the attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, paying capital costs for every added unit of power.
